Can we get comments as to "why" rather than "what"?  We're going to end up running this on every BMC reset, but I can't tell from the name if that is safe.  "SGPIO bit-83" isn't particularly useful because I should be able to figure that out from the device tree.
We will remove it.
remove it from Patchset 9.

It's rather surprising that we're using a pgood from the CPU as a reaction that we feed back out via another GPIO.  Why isn't the CPLD handling this?  The BMC isn't always guaranteed to be active, so it shouldn't really be responsible for passing signals around between hardware.
We use this pin just to sync the power status and trigger assert-power-good-drop and deassert-power-good-drop for status change.

We only use this pin for power status synchronization and internal event handling; the CPLD still manages the hardware signal logic. The BMC doesn’t relay or gate any physical signals—it just updates the internal power state when a power-good drop is detected.
It isn't clear you're actually using or configuring this.  Is this really something we're using?
We will remove it.
